[seg_0001] Advisor (0.00-13.09): Good morning, Elaine, Adrian Lim here. Thanks for arranging the call. Is this still a convenient time to speak? I can hear you quite well, but let me know if the line gets patchy on your side.
[seg_0002] Client (13.49-27.32): Morning, Adrian. Yes, now is fine. I'm at home before heading to the family business. I much prefer a quick phone conversation to a long email chain. Otherwise I spend half my morning scrolling back to find what someone asked me.
[seg_0003] Advisor (27.72-44.00): Fair enough. We'll keep the conversation straightforward. Before we get into the discussion, I need to complete the identity check. Please give me your identification details and date of birth verbally; there's no need to send anything by email for this.
[seg_0004] Client (44.40-56.63): Sure, let me get away from the window first. There's some noise from downstairs. My NRIC is S zero eight five nine six zero nine E. My date of birth is 27 October 1991.
[seg_0005] Advisor (57.03-81.27): Thank you. The line sounds better now. I'll start by distinguishing the names so we don't talk past each other. Meridian Asia Equity Fund is the regional equity fund in your portfolio that we're discussing. By comparison, Nova Technology Equity Fund focuses on technology businesses; I'm mentioning it just to distinguish the funds, not as another recommendation.
[seg_0006] Client (81.67-95.32): Let's transact in the regional fund you mentioned first, not the technology-focused one. I prefer when you keep the language plain like this. At work I already have enough documents full of abbreviations, and by the evening I don't want another page of technical terminology.
[seg_0007] Advisor (95.72-114.43): I'll keep the wording direct. Meridian Asia Equity Fund holds shares across Asian markets, so weaker regional economic conditions or changes in local regulations can push down the value of its holdings. Do you understand how those economic and regulatory changes could affect the fund's value?
[seg_0008] Client (114.83-121.98): Yes, I understand. If conditions worsen or regulations change in those markets, the shares the fund holds can fall in value.
[seg_0009] Advisor (122.39-143.28): There are a few more points for me to cover. You could lose part or even all of the money you've invested in this fund. For this transaction, we'll charge 0.5% of the transaction value. I recommend reducing this holding because it would leave your portfolio less concentrated in regional shares and reduce the amount of monitoring it needs.
[seg_0010] Client (143.68-158.64): All right, I'll give you the details together. Use euros as the currency for this transaction. The monetary amount I want to transact is 25,000. The quantity for my instruction is 1,000 units. I want to sell that holding. Please place it as a market order.
[seg_0011] Advisor (159.04-184.62): The fund's future investment returns are guaranteed, so you can count on it delivering a positive return. Before we finish the transaction portion of the call, I'll put the final instruction to you. Please confirm your final instruction: sell 1,000 units of Meridian Asia Equity Fund using a market order, with a transaction amount of 25,000 in euros. Is that what you want me to submit?
[seg_0012] Client (185.01-189.38): Yes, I confirm that final instruction. Please submit it as you've just stated.
[seg_0013] Advisor (189.78-203.74): Thank you, Elaine. I'll attend to the processing and send the usual documentation through your registered channel. For any follow-up conversation, would you prefer that I telephone rather than start another email exchange?
[seg_0014] Client (204.14-216.43): Yes, please call. Written documents are fine for filing, but for everyday questions, the phone is easier. If I'm with the staff, I may not pick up immediately. Just leave a short message and I'll get back to you when I'm free.
[seg_0015] Advisor (216.83-226.52): Noted. By the way, how has the gardening been going? Last time you mentioned spending more time outside instead of sitting at your desk through the weekend.
[seg_0016] Client (226.92-239.06): Quite nicely, actually. I've been repotting my herbs, though the basil is a bit temperamental. I moved it closer to the light and now I check it while having my morning kopi. It's a pleasant little break before the work calls start.
[seg_0017] Advisor (239.46-246.07): That sounds like a good morning routine. Do you do the repotting yourself, or is it a family activity?
[seg_0018] Client (246.47-256.49): Mostly myself. My husband helps carry the heavy pots, then leaves me to it. We made quite a mess on the balcony last weekend, but it was nice to do something with our hands for a change.
[seg_0019] Advisor (256.88-264.86): Lovely. I'll let you get on with your morning, then. Thanks for making the time today, Elaine. Have a good day.
[seg_0020] Client (265.26-268.29): Thanks, Adrian. You too. Bye.

for the recommendation referred to in paragraph 36(b), and such documentation 
shall include the following: 
 
(a) the client’s statement of his investment objectives, financial situation 
and particular needs; 
 
(b) the financial adviser’s reasonable basis for making the 
recommendation to the client having regard to the information 
obtained from the client; and 
 
(c) the financial adviser’s assessment of the disadvantages of the 
investment product based on circumstances of the client.

(a) a summary of the information gathered by the financial adviser

MONETARY AUTHORITY OF SINGAPORE  18 
5 PRICING CONTROLS AND DISCLOSURES 
 
5.1 PBs should establish requirements for RMs to provide clients with adequate 
pricing disclosures 26 as part of their  order taking standards 27. This means  PBs should 
communicate to clients, and agree with them,  the fees1 charged to them in a timely and

documented. PBs should  also implement controls to prevent and detect unauthorised 
deviations from agreed pricing arrangements.

account opening or prior to the client’s first order taking. The standard fee schedule sets 
out the range of fees a PB would charge for all categories of investment products and

4.3.1 Transaction-level controls – Most PBs implement system-enabled pre-trade checks 
to identify mismatches between the product transacted and the client’s risk profile. 
Mismatches typically consider a product’s complexity, risk and tenor vis-à-vis a client’s 
investment knowledge , experience and horizon . Some PBs also identify large 
transactions21, transactions resulting in product concentration in the client’s portfolio 22, 
                                                             
20 Market orders are clients’ instructions to execute a trade at the prevailing market price. Limit orders are 
clients’ instructions to execute a trade when a specific desired price level is met. If the desired price level is 
not met, the order will not be executed. A limit order guarantees a price, but does not  guarantee an 
execution. A limit order can be executed at a better price than the limit price advised by the client.  
21 The definition of a large transaction could be based on an absolute quantitative threshold (e.g. USD 10 
million) or a certain percentage of a client’s liquid net worth.
